name: Incident Center
description: Coordinate production incidents, their responders and timelines, and the postmortems that follow
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may read the public stats; require auth for reading, opening and updating incidents, posting timeline events and reading postmortem previews; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
Incidents: any signed-in user may open an incident and update any incident; incidents are never deleted

Incident validation: title (at most 200 characters) and service_name (at most 100 characters) are required non-empty strings; severity is one of sev1, sev2, sev3, sev4; impact_summary, when given, is at most 2000 characters; commander, when given, is a non-empty string of at most 50 characters naming the responder (normally a username; it is not checked against the accounts) and defaults to the signed-in user's username
A new incident starts in status investigating with opened_at set to the creation time and opened_by set to the signed-in user's username

PATCH /api/incidents/:id changes only the fields it is given (title, service_name, severity, status, commander, impact_summary, postmortem_completed); status is one of investigating, mitigated, monitoring, resolved and may move in any direction

Status changes set the timestamps: mitigated_at is set the first time an incident reaches mitigated, monitoring or resolved; resolved_at is set when it becomes resolved; moving a resolved incident to any other status is a reopen that clears resolved_at and adds 1 to reopen_count
Every status change made through PATCH appends a status_change timeline event authored by the signed-in user whose message names the old and new status (for example "investigating -> mitigated")

SLA: the resolution target is 60 minutes for sev1, 240 for sev2, 1440 for sev3 and 4320 for sev4; sla_due_at is opened_at plus the target of the current severity, and sla_breached is true when the incident was resolved after sla_due_at or is still unresolved past it

GET /api/incidents returns incidents newest opened first; ?severity=, ?status= and ?service_name= match exactly, ?commander= matches the commander username, ?open=true keeps only unresolved incidents, ?query= matches title, service_name or impact_summary case-insensitively, ?page= and ?page_size= page the result (page_size default 20, at most 100), and total counts every matching incident

Timeline: POST /api/incidents/:id/timeline appends an event of type acknowledgement, mitigation, escalation, recovery, customer_update or note with a required message of at most 2000 characters, authored by the signed-in user; status_change events are only created by the server; posting an event does not change the incident's status; GET /api/incidents/:id/timeline lists events oldest first
Customer updates are the timeline events of type customer_update

GET /api/public/stats returns open_total, open_by_severity (an object with a count for each of sev1 to sev4), sla_breached_open, resolved_last_30_days, and mttr_minutes (the mean of resolved_at minus opened_at in minutes over incidents resolved in the last 30 days, rounded to one decimal, null when there are none)

GET /api/incidents/:id/postmortem-preview assembles a draft without storing anything: the incident's fields, duration_minutes (resolved_at or now minus opened_at, whole minutes), the full timeline oldest first, and draft, a plain-text summary with the title, severity, service, duration, impact summary and one line per timeline event
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-admin on admin endpoints, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Operations landing page for everyone with the public stats (open incidents by severity, SLA breaches, resolved in 30 days, MTTR); signed-in users also see cards for the open incidents, and visitors see a 'Sign in to respond to incidents' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out

Incident browser: a table with severity, title, service, status, commander, opened time and an SLA badge (on track, breached), filters for severity and status, an open-only switch, a search box and previous/next paging
Open-incident form (title, service, severity, optional impact summary and commander) that shows the API's validation messages

Incident detail page: the incident's fields, controls to change status, severity and commander, the timeline oldest first with a form to post an event, and a separate customer update feed showing only customer_update events
Responder dashboard: the signed-in user's open incidents as commander (?commander=<username>&open=true), with SLA-breached ones highlighted as overdue
Postmortem preview page that shows the assembled draft for an incident and lets a responder mark the postmortem completed
admin_requirements: Admin audit view: every incident with its reopen count and postmortem status, plus counts of open sev1 incidents, incidents ever reopened and postmortems due

Postmortems due are resolved sev1 and sev2 incidents whose postmortem_completed is false; show avg_mitigation_minutes (mean of mitigated_at minus opened_at over incidents that have mitigated_at, rounded to one decimal, null when there are none)

data_models.name: Incident
data_models.description: A production incident; sla_due_at, sla_breached and timeline_count are computed

fields.title: string (required, max 200 chars)
fields.severity: string (one of: sev1, sev2, sev3, sev4)
fields.status: string (one of: investigating, mitigated, monitoring, resolved; default investigating)
fields.commander: string (username, max 50 chars; defaults to the user who opened it)
fields.opened_by: string (username of the signed-in user who opened it)
fields.mitigated_at: datetime (nullable; first time the status left investigating)

data_models.name: TimelineEvent
data_models.description: One entry in an incident's response timeline

fields.event_type: string (one of: acknowledgement, mitigation, escalation, recovery, customer_update, note, status_change; status_change is server-created)
fields.author: string (username of the signed-in user who posted it)
